name: WENO5-Z (q = 1), finite-difference flux form
source: Borges, Carmona, Costa and Don, J. Comput. Phys. 227 (2008) 3191-3211: alpha_k = d_k (1 + (tau_5/(beta_k + eps))^q), tau_5 = |beta_0 - beta_2|, Jiang-Shu beta_k. The paper itself was not accessible to us (paywalled); its statements are taken from secondary sources: q = 1 gives 4th order at first-order critical points and q = 2 gives 5th, a numerical finding of the 2008 paper for the derivative approximation, eps = 1e-40 (arXiv 2004.07954 sec. 2.2; arXiv 2110.13607 sec. 2.2; R. Borges, PhD thesis, UFRJ 2014, pp. 61, 70); the eps family: Don and Borges, J. Comput. Phys. 250 (2013) 347-372, as summarised in the same thesis (p. 70) and in W. S. Don's 2018 slides (slides 16-19: tau_5 = |a14 f' f'''' + a23 f'' f'''| dx^5 + ..., and for q = 1 at n_cp = 1 fifth order needs eps >= c dx^m with m <= 3)

claims.why: f' != 0: beta_k = (f' dx)^2 (1 + O(dx^2)) and tau_5 = O(dx^5) (Borges et al. per the thesis p. 61), so tau/beta_k = O(dx^3), omega_k = d_k + O(dx^3): the error is that of the linear weights, O(dx^5)
the linear part has a non-zero dx^5 term
as for one reconstruction, with weight errors O(dx^3) at both stencils: O(dx^3) dx^3 / dx = O(dx^5)
the linear part has a non-zero dx^5 term
f' = 0: every beta_k = (13/12) f''^2 dx^4 (1 + O(dx)) and tau_5 = O(dx^5), so tau/beta_k = c dx + O(dx^2) with c the same for every k; then omega_k - d_k = O(dx^2), times candidate errors O(dx^3)
weight errors O(dx^2) at both stencils (at x_{i-1} the leading beta_k are still common, f' = -f'' dx gives beta_k = O(dx^4) with tau = O(dx^5)), so each face error is O(dx^5): O(dx^5)/dx

Borges et al. (2008) report 4th order at first-order critical points with q = 1 (secondary sources, numerical, eps = 1e-40); our sketch: the O(dx^2) weight errors of the two stencils differ, so the dx^5 face errors do not cancel in the difference. Not derived to the coefficient

Don and Borges (2013) per the thesis and slides: for q = 1 at n_cp = 1, eps = Omega(dx^m) with m <= 3 gives fifth order. Sketch: eps + beta_k = dx^3 (1 + O(dx)) for every k, tau/(eps + beta_k) = O(dx^2) with a common leading term, so omega_k - d_k = O(dx^3)
eps comparable to beta_k = O(dx^4): as eps = 0 (m = 4 > 3, outside the Don-Borges range), so order 4
eps fixed: beta = O(dx^4) << eps, omega_k - d_k = O(dx^5)
convex weights (all alpha_k > 0) of third-order candidates: each face error O(dx^3), so the difference is O(dx^2)

the thesis (p. 70) says all three schemes (WENO-JS, -M, -Z) lose accuracy at critical points of order 2 (with q = 2, eps = 1e-40); at n_cp = 2 the leading beta_k differ, (121/108, 1/36, 121/108) f'''^2 dx^6. The exact order is not derived
